title: Team AI training for medical practices | Creosote Labs
meta_description: A one-day, hands-on AI workshop for medical practice staff, run on the practice's own templates and tools. $1,000 per person, 5-person minimum.
h1: Team AI training for medical practices
intro: The people in a medical practice who spend the most time writing are usually not the physicians. Front-desk staff, medical assistants, billers, and the office manager produce patient letters, appeal responses to denied claims, policy updates, job postings, and answers to the same portal questions every week, most of it in Word, Outlook, or Google Docs. Many practices already pay for Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace and have Copilot or Gemini available without using either for this work.

Creosote Labs runs a one-day workshop, on site or remote, in the AI tool the practice already licenses. Each participant works on their own computer with their own documents: a biller drafts an appeal from a real denial, a medical assistant turns clinical instructions into a patient handout, the office manager rewrites the phone policy. Everyone leaves with a working setup, documents their own process, and receives a written guide. A 30-day follow-up is included, and the day covers what may and may not go into each tool.
projects: A denied-claim appeal letter drafted by the biller from the denial notice and the practice's appeal template, then reviewed against payer rules.
A patient handout produced by a medical assistant from the clinician's discharge instructions, checked for reading level and accuracy.
A set of saved reply templates for the most common portal messages, written by front-desk staff and stored in the team's shared drive.
An updated employee handbook section rewritten by the office manager from the current version and a list of policy changes.
A weekly summary of open tasks generated from the practice's existing spreadsheet exports, set up by whoever owns that report.

faqs.q: Can staff use these tools with patient information?
faqs.a: Yes, but only in tools the practice has a business associate agreement for, which we confirm before the workshop. Exercises are built so participants learn the process on their real documents without putting protected health information anywhere it does not belong.

faqs.q: How many people can attend and what does it cost?
faqs.a: The workshop is $1,000 per person for up to 10 people, with a 5-person minimum. Larger teams are quoted, and travel is included. A program with three monthly follow-up sessions is $1,400 per person.

No. The workshop is designed for whoever produces the practice's written work, which is usually the front desk, billing, clinical support staff, and the office manager. Physicians are welcome, and clinical documentation can be included if the practice wants it.
